Complex-linear star paired with conjugation gives the determinant Hermitian metric. In dimension zero the complex orientation is positive, star=identity, positive-degree spaces and operators vanish; finite empty sums work. Read all eight actual prerequisites and four complete proof steps. Normal holomorphic coordinates are justified by closedness symmetry and a quadratic holomorphic map with identity Jacobian; differentiated the transformed metric and checked the factor 2 from h(0)=I/2. Metric/density first derivatives vanish so the local adjoint formula in orthonormal frames agrees at the point with the coordinate coframe formula (normalizing its constant norm only changes notation). Creation/contraction anticommutators with norm-square 2 give all four commutator signs. Direct expansion of graded Jacobi and square-zero identities gives both mixed anticommutators zero and equality of the two complex Laplacians; d* is their sum. L commutes with partial and dbar by closed omega, and adjunction supplies Lambda commutation. Derived the degree-dependent star identities from Stokes and star-square; they exchange the two Laplacian summands and make their sum commute. Bidegrees and endpoints follow from orthogonality and the shifts (0,+/-1); n=0 and zero forms are disposed explicitly. Compactness makes the tested smooth sections compactly supported and there is no boundary term. Full AC supplies countable choice for adjoint/integration/Stokes conventions, while the local coordinate and finite exterior computations are choice-free. Independently read Schnell Class 14 Lemma 14.7 and complete proof, pp.3–4, https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~cschnell/mat545/class14.pdf; Class 18 Corollaries 18.1–18.2 with proofs, p.1, https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~cschnell/mat545/class18.pdf.
